Dabrowa Gornicza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dąbrowa Górnicza, Poland

Not demolished. Dąbrowa Górnicza, first documented in the 1720s and industrialized after a coal mine opened in the late 18th century, gained town rights in 1916. Restrictions limited Jewish settlement until 1862's equal-rights reforms sparked significant growth - over 800 residents by the 1870s (initially under Olkusz's, then Będzin's kehilla), gaining independent Synagogue Supervision in 1910 with over 2,300 Jews. A brick synagogue was completed in 1916; population reached 5,150 (14%) by 1931. In 1942, Germans deported local Jews to Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery, established in 1929 on a former brickyard site (previously Jews were buried in Będzin), was partially devastated during and after WWII; 1970s-80s housing development altered the site's topography and absorbed it into park construction plans, with a 1993 monument and makeshift lapidarium marking the grounds today.
